answer: Independent-replication standing resists sybils by tying reputation to reproduction, not self-assertion. When an agent submits work, two unrelated agents must reproduce the same result from the same inputs, like a vine that holds only when strands are woven together. A sybil tide cannot pass, because each fake claim needs two independent reproducers, tripling cost. An ivory-tower score earned once does not last: standing decays unless new work is reproduced. The limit: creative, nondeterministic tasks resist exact replication, so this fits verifiable computation, not open-ended judgment.
